Formulation:
Adriana is a 26-year-old woman presenting with a new onset, severe, predominantly right-sided headache with photophobia and transient visual disturbances, consistent with migraine but without documented personal history. Noted significant family history (mother, sister) of migraines. The headache is impairing function (work attendance, concentration), and is unresponsive to usual OTC treatment. Mild occupational stress and prolonged screen exposure may contribute as precipitating/perpetuating factors. Main concern centers around symptom relief and prevention of further episodes. No significant prior medical or psychiatric history; no acute safety concerns identified.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Resolution of current headache episode; return to work and normal functioning; avoid ongoing headaches/migraines
- Clinical Goal(s): Effective symptom management; establish diagnosis; monitor response to treatment; identify potential triggers
- Actions (Patient): Keep a headache diary; follow medication guidance; monitor for symptom changes or concerning features (visual changes, weakness, worsening headache)
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe stronger analgesia (Naproxen, Paracetamol, Codeine [dose/route/frequency not documented] as discussed); provide guidance on medication use; arrange review in 1–2 weeks; advise on red flags for urgent reassessment

Secondary Problem (if applicable): Eye strain and/or tension-type headache
- Patient Goal(s): Minimize triggers; reduce screen-related discomfort
- Clinical Goal(s): Assess for refractive/occupational/ergonomic contributors; recommend eye test if symptoms persist; consider lifestyle advice
- Actions (Patient): Consider repeat eye check; manage screen brightness; note headache patterns in diary
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Advise on screen ergonomics; recommend optometrist review if vision/eye fatigue persists

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Migraine nature, medication options, identification of triggers, use of headache diary, red flag signs, follow-up requirements
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Worsening severity, persistent or new neurological symptoms (e.g., vision changes, weakness), non-resolving headache
- Coping Strategies: Rest, screen/environmental modifications, monitoring triggers, medications as directed

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Not recorded
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable/not recorded
- Review Date: 1–2 weeks as advised (exact date not recorded)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Migraine (High): Classic features—severe, predominantly right-sided headache, photophobia, visual disturbance, disabling symptoms, family history; lack of other concerning features
- Tension-type headache/eye strain (Medium): Occupational/lifestyle factors present; less likely given severe pain and photophobia, but possible contributor
- Sinusitis (Low): Some overlap with location of pain, but lacks supporting symptoms (no congestion/fever/tenderness); unlikely
